item.title: US Mid-Term Election Result 2026 LIVE: Republicans or Democrats — Who’ll control Senate? First results start coming in
item.description: US Mid-Term Election Result 2026 LIVE: Polling stations began to close in Indiana and Kentucky at 6 pm ET (2300 GMT), with Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia and most of Florida following suit at 7 pm. Stay tuned to this LIVE blog for all the latest updates on US midterm election results.
item.dc:creator: Akriti Anand
item.content:encoded: US Midterm Election Result 2026 LIVE: Will US President Donald Trump's Republican Party retain power in the US House athe nd Senate? Americans went to the polls on Tuesday (November 3) to decide who controls Congress.Polling stations began to close in Indiana and Kentucky at 6 pm ET (2300 GMT), with Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia and most of Florida following suit at 7 pm.The results, held two years after presidential elections, will determine how much legislative power US President Donald Trump's administration retains during the remainder of his term (which ends in 2028).Is voting over? When will results start coming in?The first US midterm results are expected from around 4:30 am IST on Wednesday, November 4, corresponding to 6 pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on Tuesday.According to Reuters, polls closed in seven states on Tuesday as millions of Americans cast ballots to determine whether to strip control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans.State-wise details: The first polls close at 6 pm ET (4:30 am IST) Tuesday in parts of Indiana and Kentucky, followed by 7 pm in states including Georgia, Virginia and South Carolina. Polls close at 7:30 pm (6:00 am IST) in North Carolina and Ohio, followed by a large group of states at 8 pm (6:30 am IST), including Pennsylvania and Maine as well as most of Texas and Michigan. Voting ends at 9 pm (7:30 am IST) in battleground states including Arizona and Wisconsin, along with the remaining parts of Texas and Michigan. Polls in Nevada close at 10 pm (8:30 am IST) Eastern, followed by California and several other western states at 11 pm (9:30 am IST). The final polling places, in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands, close at 1 am ET (11:30 am) on Wednesday.What have exit polls shown?According to exit polls, Democrats are favored to capture the House and both parties may be locked in an intense state-by-state battle for the Senate.Voters rebuked Trump and his agenda, blaming him for stubbornly high prices, with a large majority unhappy about the direction of the country, according to voter exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets that included major television networks and the Associated Press.The exit polls reflected upon electorates' overwhelmingly sour mood, showing half of voters said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the way the country is headed.Many reportedly said they feel worse off than when Trump entered the White House in 2025. Nearly 9 in 10 identified the cost of living as a crucial or major factor in their vote, signaling that the elections could prove a repudiation of Trump and his Republican Party.Why are US midterm elections held?Midterm elections are typically seen as a referendum on the president, and that is particularly true for Trump, who dominates attention like no other modern politician. Trump himself has told his supporters to "pretend I'm on the ballot," a message Democratic leaders have happily echoed.

item.title: Learjet Parts Found Miles from Florida Crash Site, NTSB Says
item.description: Parts of the private jet that crashed in Florida on Sunday killing nine people were found miles from the impact site, suggesting they broke off before the plane hit the ground, according to US air safety investigators.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Parts of the private jet that crashed in Florida on Sunday killing nine people were found miles from the impact site, suggesting they broke off before the plane hit the ground, according to US air safety investigators. Most of the Learjet 60’s left elevator was located in three pieces within a range of about 1.3 to 3.8 miles from the crash site, US National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman told reporters Tuesday. The elevator is located on the tail of the aircraft and controls whether the nose is pointed up or down.“Knowing that it was lost is a very important piece of evidence in terms of pointing us towards other things to investigate,” Chapman said. The distance suggests it broke off before impact but the NTSB is still trying to determine if losing the piece contributed to the accident or if it was the result of forces on the plane when it began plummeting toward the ground. Investigators have been digging into what caused the fatal crash in Palm Beach County, Florida. In communications with air traffic controllers, one of the pilots of the Learjet 60 reported moderate turbulence, ice and precipitation. The aircraft briefly climbed before nosediving at a high speed. The crash created a large crater on a roadway. The NTSB previously said weather conditions are a major focus of its investigation. A public relations firm for the families of the crash victims said technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson was on the flight with his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two children. The children’s caretaker, Anita Maria Cetina, as well as Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, were also among the passengers, the joint statement said. News outlets have reported that the pilots of the aircraft were 55-year-old Jeff Gregory and 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras. Authorities haven’t publicly confirmed the victims’ identities, but Chapman said Tuesday that NTSB was aware of the names of the victims and “keeping them in our thoughts.”More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
